Pick a new look for InfoDeck

Four complete, colourful directions. Each option redraws all 20 screens — lock, home, search, sheets, card view, editor, reminders, sharing, QR, file rename, upcoming, categories, tags, settings, text size, error logs and the erase dialog.

Design only — nothing is built until you choose an option and say “build”.

1

Option 1 · Aurora Pop

Vivid gradient headers, airy white cards, glossy gradient tiles, floating pill navigation.

Signature: Role-coloured gradient header on every screen; gradient glyph tiles; glass stat pills.

Palette
Type: Poppins
Navigation: Floating pill bar, gradient bubble on active tab
Build effort: Low–medium
SrNo.Why it works
1Closest evolution of today's indigo identity — lowest learning curve
2Gradients add energy without hurting readability (white cards carry the text)
3Role colour per screen header makes every page instantly recognisable
4Cheapest to build: Material 3 components + Brush gradients
SrNo.Watch-outs
1Gradients everywhere can feel busy if over-used — needs discipline
2Less distinctive than options 2 and 4
2

Option 2 · Candy Blocks

Playful neo-brutal: bold flat candy colours, thick ink outlines, hard offset shadows, chunky tap targets.

Signature: 2 px ink outlines + 3 px offset shadows; flat pastel category blocks; tilted stat stickers.

Palette
Type: Space Grotesk
Navigation: Boxed bar, active tab is a yellow sticker block
Build effort: Medium–high
SrNo.Why it works
1Most fun and memorable — every element is a big, obvious, colourful target
2Thick outlines give excellent contrast and glanceability (great for Easy-read mode)
3Flat colours print, screenshot and QR-share cleanly
4Strong personality that sets InfoDeck apart from stock Material apps
SrNo.Watch-outs
1Bold style is a matter of taste — may feel 'toy-like' for ID/insurance data
2Needs a custom component layer (borders + offset shadows) over Material 3
3Dark theme needs its own careful variant
3

Option 3 · Neon Night

Dark-first: deep navy glass surfaces with neon cyan, magenta, lime and amber glows.

Signature: Neon glyph tiles with glow; gradient-text titles; glowing countdown rings on due items.

Palette
Type: DM Sans
Navigation: Glass bar, neon underline glow on active tab
Build effort: Medium
SrNo.Why it works
1Stunning in the evening and on OLED — saves battery
2Neon accents keep it very colourful while the dark base stays calm
3Glow is a natural 'attention' signal for overdue and due-soon items
4Feels premium and secure — fits a vault of documents
SrNo.Watch-outs
1Dark-only character: the light theme becomes a secondary, less exciting mode
2Glow/blur effects cost more GPU on older phones (fallback: flat tints)
3Neon on dark needs careful contrast checks for small text
4

Option 4 · Sunrise Wallet

Warm cream canvas, cards drawn as real gradient wallet cards, rounded friendly type, centre New button.

Signature: Every card is a gradient wallet card; greeting header; OVERDUE stamp; centre ＋ button.

Palette
Type: Fredoka headings + Nunito body
Navigation: Curved bar with raised centre ＋ New card
Build effort: Medium–high
SrNo.Why it works
1The metaphor fits perfectly: InfoDeck *is* a wallet of cards — instantly understood
2Each category's card has its own gradient, so the list is a colourful deck
3Big centre '+' button makes adding a card the obvious action
4Warm, friendly tone suits a personal, family-use app
SrNo.Watch-outs
1Gradient wallet cards take more height — fewer cards per screen in Comfortable
2White text on lighter gradients (yellow/teal) needs a shade guard
3Most rework of the Home row component

C · What stays the same in every option

SrNo.Standard / requirementHow every option honours it
125 % bottom clearance on every sheet and dialog (NFR-5)Hatched SheetBottomSpace zone drawn in frames 05, 06, 09, 11, 12 and 20
2Settings = named accordion, all collapsed, one open at a time (FR-6.1)Frames 16, 17, 20 show exactly one group open; colour tile per group
3About Me ultra-compact-B — last, never collapsible (FR-6.2)Header strip → KB identity + LinkedIn/Facebook → Suggestion/Feedback/Bug/Error + Send → mail caption → two-line footer
4Editor chrome: Cancel/Discard outlined + Save filled, equal width, one row (FR-6.6)Frames 08, 09, 12, 18; sheets use Cancel + Apply / Rename / Save
5Destructive actions never on a first surface; typed ERASE / DELETE (FR-6.5)Danger zone… link at the end of card view & editor; Erase dialog with Erase disabled until ERASE is typed
6Role hues keep their meaning (design 1.5.D1)Amber = time, rose = trouble, green = share/OK, purple = file, violet = tag/QR, teal = settings, sky = data — only the tones change per option
7Home: accordion, countdown ring, overdue washed rose, tap-to-expand Open · Edit · Share (FR-3.x)Frame 02 in every option; overdue row = Bike Insurance
8Search reads every field, hit highlighted, kind badges (FR-4.x)Frame 04 — “wb24” matches WB 24 AB 1234 in data and a file name
9Share field picker, masking, live preview, files after text (FR-5.x)Frame 10 — masked Vehicle No, 2 files ready line, coloured send targets
10Offline by default (NFR-1)Lock screen says so; the update card (17) appears only once the GitHub update checker spec is approved
11AccessibilityEvery option keeps ≥ 48 dp tap targets, text never relies on colour alone (labels + icons), works with Text size 70–200 %

D · Recommendation

SrNo.PickReasoning
1Recommended: Option 4 · Sunrise WalletMost colourful and easiest to understand: InfoDeck already is a deck of cards, so drawing each one as a wallet card makes the Home list self-explanatory; the centre ＋ makes adding a card obvious
2Safer alternative: Option 1 · Aurora PopKeeps today's indigo identity and layout, so it is the quickest to build with the least retraining — but it is the least distinctive
3Bold choice: Option 2 · Candy BlocksHighest contrast and fun; best if you want the app to look unlike any other — taste-dependent for ID / insurance data
4Night choice: Option 3 · Neon NightChoose if you mostly use the phone in the evening or on OLED; light theme would need its own design pass

F · If an option is approved

SrNo.StepWhat happens
1You pickReply with the option number (or a mix) and answers to Q1–Q7 — “defaults” accepts every recommended default

3QueueItem added to BACKLOG with its three companions — exception handling, Logger.e logging, JUnit + device checklist
4Build only on triggerNothing is built, versioned or released until you say “build” / “release”; then 1.16.0 via a cld- pull request
